name: Hanok K-Beauty
address: 520 S San Vicente Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90048
what_it_is: A Korean skincare spa and facial studio that also sells Korean skincare products. It is a treatment-focused spa rather than a walk-in cosmetics store.
facts: It is a roughly 4,500 sq ft Korean facial spa built around 'glass skin' facials and naturally derived products.
Services listed include Glass Skin, acne-prone skin, anti-aging, PDRN and couples facials, with skin analysis using high-definition imaging and 3D mapping.
Visits can include a Korean tea ceremony with teas sourced from Jeju Island and a Hanbok (traditional Korean dress) wardrobe fitting.
It has three VIP private rooms and two couples rooms.
Korean skincare products are sold on site.
There is a private parking lot at 500 S San Vicente Blvd at the top of the block.
price: Spa pricing; one listed 90-minute facial is $250
hours_note: Apple Maps listing shows weekday hours 10:00 AM-8:00 PM; weekend hours unclear (confirm on official site)
booking_note: Facial treatments are appointment-based; book through the official site or call (213) 782-6690

name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul Thrift Store (Los Angeles)
what_it_is: A huge donation-based thrift store run by the Society of St. Vincent de Paul Council of Los Angeles. Room after room of used clothing, furniture and household goods at bargain prices.
facts: The Society calls it L.A.'s largest thrift store, and travel writers describe it as packed room after room with bargains.
It sells used clothing, shoes, furniture, housewares and home goods, all donated.
Regulars say it hides odd finds in every corner, from vintage chairs to skee-ball machines.
The store moved from Chinatown to this Lincoln Heights location in 1969.
Proceeds support the Society of St. Vincent de Paul's charitable programs in Los Angeles.
hours_note: 211LA listing: Mon-Sat 9:30am-6:00pm, Sun 9:00am-5:00pm (sources conflict; call 323-226-9643 to confirm)

name: TROVE
neighborhood: West Los Angeles (Westwood Blvd, just north of Pico)
what_it_is: A consignment and thrift shop on Westwood Blvd in West LA that sells secondhand clothing, jewelry, housewares and collectibles. Stock ranges from mall brands to designer labels.
facts: It is a department-store-style consignment shop with clothing, jewelry, housewares and collectibles.
Clothing runs from Zara to Prada, and listings mention brands like Gucci, Chanel and Calvin Klein.
It describes itself as a top consignment and thrift shop in Los Angeles.
It has a free parking lot.
hours_note: Official hours page: Mon-Sat 11am-7pm, Sun 12pm-6pm (third-party listings differ slightly)

name: Lemon Frog Shop
address: 1202 N Alvarado St, Los Angeles, CA 90026
what_it_is: A tiny, maximalist vintage shop in Echo Park packed floor to ceiling with clothing and accessories, mostly from the 1950s through the 1990s. A California Certified Green Business.
facts: The shop is about the size of a walk-in closet but is stuffed floor to ceiling with rare vintage finds.
Stock covers clothing, shoes, purses, sunglasses, belts and jewelry, mostly from the 1950s through the 1990s.
The focus is women's vintage from the '50s through the '80s.
Vintage footwear often comes from Brazil, Italy and Spain.
It is known for hundreds of items priced around $10.
It is a California Certified Green Business.
hours_note: Time Out says 'call for hours'; an older Patch post listed 11:30am-7:30pm. Phone 213-413-2143.

name: Melrose Trading Post
address: 7850 Melrose Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90046 (Fairfax High School campus)
what_it_is: A Sunday flea market held every week on the Fairfax High School campus with vintage clothing, handmade goods, art, food and live music. Proceeds fund arts programs at Fairfax High.
facts: It runs every Sunday, rain or shine, on the Fairfax High School campus at Melrose and Fairfax.
Vendors sell vintage clothing, handmade goods, art, antiques and food, with live music.
Proceeds fund the Greenway Institute for the Arts, which provides free in-school and after-school arts programs for Fairfax High and LAUSD students.
Students 13+ with a school ID get $1 off in-person admission.
The market also supports Greenway Court Theatre, a professional theatre on the campus.
Every December Sunday it becomes the 'Merry Melrose' holiday edition.
price: $6 cash admission at the gate ($6 + $2.25 fee for online pre-paid ticket); students 13+ with school ID and seniors 65+ pay $1 less in person
hours_note: Sundays only, 10 AM-5 PM; summer hours 10 AM-6 PM Memorial Day to Labor Day; last cash ticket sold at 4:45 PM (official site, plan-your-visit page)
age_note: All ages; student discount for ages 13+ with school ID
booking_note: Walk up and pay cash at the entrance, or buy a scannable pre-paid ticket online

name: Squaresville
address: 1800 N Vermont Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90027
what_it_is: A two-story buy-sell-trade vintage clothing store in Los Feliz. You can shop racks of past-decade clothing or bring in your own secondhand pieces for cash, trade or consignment.
facts: It is a buy-sell-trade store, so you can bring in your own secondhand clothing for payment, trade or consignment.
New pieces come in daily because of the constant trade-in flow.
It is two stories, with men's and women's clothing plus accessories, handbags and shoes from past decades.
Stock covers all genders, from formalwear to T-shirts, and is popular for playful costume-style finds.
Its sister shop Urchin is a few doors down at 1766 N Vermont but does not buy or trade.
hours_note: Time Out listing: Sun-Mon noon-7pm, Tue-Thu 11am-8pm, Fri-Sat 11am-9pm (may have changed; phone (323) 669-8464)
booking_note: Walk in; bring items to sell or trade in person

name: animate Los Angeles
address: 3525 W Carson St, Suite 511, Torrance, CA 90503 (also listed as 21540 Hawthorne Blvd, Unit 511)
what_it_is: The U.S. store of animate, Japan's biggest anime retailer, inside the Del Amo Fashion Center mall. It sells manga, figures, trading cards, character goods and other anime merchandise.
facts: It is the first U.S. store of animate, Japan's largest anime merchandise chain, and opened in the Del Amo Fashion Center in summer 2023.
It carries manga, comics, light novels and art books, plus figures, trading cards, keychains, stickers and other character goods.
It stocks VTuber merchandise and game-related products, including goods from both inside and outside the U.S.
It sells Japanese snacks that come with toys.
It is in the same mall as Kinokuniya's Torrance bookstore (in Mitsuwa Marketplace), so anime shopping can be combined.
hours_note: Official store page: Mon-Fri 10:00-21:00, Sat 10:00-20:00, Sun 11:00-19:00

name: Canter's Deli
address: 419 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036
what_it_is: A famous old-school Jewish deli on Fairfax Avenue with a bakery counter and the Kibitz Room bar. It is a late-night LA landmark that has been serving pastrami and matzo ball soup since the 1930s.
facts: Canter's opened in 1931 on Brooklyn Avenue in Boyle Heights, moved to Fairfax in 1948, and since 1953 has occupied the old Esquire Theatre building, which is why the dining room is so big.
It is known for classic deli food like pastrami sandwiches and matzo ball soup, plus fresh baked goods from its bakery counter.
The attached Kibitz Room bar opened in 1961 and became a late-night musicians' hangout where Lenny Kravitz, Slash, Haim, The Kooks and Red Hot Chili Peppers have played.
It celebrated its 95th anniversary on August 3, 2026 by selling pastrami sandwiches for 95 cents, drawing hundreds of customers.
Canter's was featured in Hellmann's 2026 Super Bowl commercial.
It is on the Los Angeles Conservancy's list of historic places.
hours_note: Sources conflict: Canter's own site says it serves 24 hours a day, while an OpenTable listing shows Mon-Thu 6am-11:30pm, Fri-Sat until 5am, Sun until 11:30pm, and the Kibitz Room closes at 2am. Confirm before a late-night visit.
age_note: Restaurant is all ages; the Kibitz Room is a bar (21+)
